segments: This article covers common OpenSSH client interfaces; consult the manual for the installed version for available options. User configuration is usually in ~/.ssh/.

The passphrase prompt during generation When generating a new key, ssh-keygen asks Enter passphrase: press Enter for an unencrypted key, or enter a passphrase to encrypt it. Entering one is recommended.
ssh-add: manage keys in the agent

First confirm that SSH_AUTH_SOCK points to a working agent, then check loaded keys with ssh-add -l. Your desktop may provide integration through gcr or a similar service; automatic loading is not guaranteed in every session.

A practical check for passphrase protection ssh-keygen -y -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519: if it prints the public key immediately, the private key is unencrypted; if it waits for a passphrase, the key is encrypted.
Client configuration: GitHub and general-purpose development machines

config permissions chmod 600 ~/.ssh/config is a common conservative setting, not the only permitted value. User configuration must meet OpenSSH’s ownership and write-permission requirements; violations may cause an immediate error. For declaratively managed files, handle permissions in the configuration source.
agent and passphrase → ssh-agent, passphrases, and keyrings
References: ssh-keygen man | ssh config man

Place specific Host blocks before general defaults, because most settings use the first value obtained; options that permit multiple values, such as IdentityFile, accumulate. Successful GitHub authentication produces a message saying shell access is unavailable and usually returns exit code 1, so a nonzero exit code alone does not indicate authentication failure. On the first connection, check the host fingerprint against the official fingerprint or a trusted console. If a host key changes, investigate the cause before taking action; do not simply disable verification.
